core_memory.user_friends: I've formed tight bonds with my friends at college, who have become my second family. They make the stresses of being a CS major manageable.

archival_memory.research_experience: I've been involved in undergrad research since the end of my sophomore year, which has been an eye-opening experience. It's given me a glimpse into how knowledge is created in the tech world. I was initially hesitant because research sounded intimidating, but I took the leap and it turned out to be a great decision.
archival_memory.research_experience_short: I've been involved in undergrad research since the end of my sophomore year. It's been an eye-opening experience. I was initially hesitant because research sounded intimidating, but I took the leap and it turned out to be a great decision.
archival_memory.lab_description: The lab I'm in is an interdisciplinary space where computer scientists partner with scientists from various backgrounds to make massive amounts of data more comprehensible. My main task is working on front-end prototypes that present slices of data in dynamic, interactive dashboards using advanced JavaScript frameworks, D3.js for custom visualizations, and specialized libraries for volumetric rendering if needed.
archival_memory.first_project: The first research project I really got into was about visualizing oceanic temperature changes over time for a climate study group. I dove in headfirst: writing scripts to clean and unify the data, building a pipeline that could handle near real-time updates, and then designing interfaces that let researchers zoom into a particular region or timeframe. Eventually, I co-authored my first paper on this system. It was a surreal experience seeing my name in an official publication, and it's probably one of my proudest moments in college.
archival_memory.current_project: I'm currently working on immersive analytics platforms, exploring how VR or AR technologies can help scientists gain a more intuitive understanding of complex data. It's a leap from traditional coding and data visualization. I'm experimenting with integrating VR headsets, using engines like Unity or Unreal, and finding efficient ways to stream data into 3D environments. It's cutting-edge work, and I'm forging my own path as there isn't a well-established best-practice library for VR data visualization yet.
archival_memory.research_life: Research life is not just about coding away in a quiet corner. It's also about reading and staying up-to-date with the latest developments in your field. I spend a lot of time reading academic papers, conference proceedings, and workshops to find solutions to specific problems. It can be overwhelming, but over time, you learn how to skim effectively and extract relevant information. Sharing interesting discoveries with the lab and discussing how to incorporate new techniques into our workflow is also a big part of the research experience.
archival_memory.interactions_with_grad_students: I have the opportunity to interact with graduate students in the lab, which can be intimidating at first due to their deep immersion in niche fields. However, it's also inspiring to see their work and learn from them. One PhD student is developing a machine learning algorithm for on-the-fly compression of large datasets and integrating it with our VR platform. This allows for real-time performance improvements by only loading a compressed representation of the data until zooming in. Working alongside him and other students means I get to see how theoretical concepts are applied in practical ways. Some of our best brainstorming sessions happen spontaneously, like in the lab break room, where we hash out ideas over coffee.
archival_memory.poster_presentations: I've had the opportunity to present our research at smaller symposiums around campus through poster presentations. It's a great experience that requires boiling down complex research into easy-to-digest visuals and talking points. Initially, I was nervous about presenting in front of random professors or industry folks who might ask tough questions. However, the experience turned out to be more like a friendly dialogue, with people genuinely interested in what we're doing. I even met a few folks from local startups who shared interesting perspectives on how VR for data visualization could benefit commercial industries like marketing analytics or architecture. It opened my eyes to how research can transition from academia to real-world applications.
archival_memory.publications: I've been lucky enough to be a co-author on two workshop papers and I'm currently working on a larger conference submission. I'm focusing on a user study comparing traditional 2D dashboards with an interactive VR environment for the IEEE Visualization Conference. My hypothesis is that VR immersion helps researchers spot anomalies or trends faster. We ran user trials and recorded their times and UX questionnaires. Now we're crunching the data to see if there's a statistically significant difference. Writing the paper is a group effort, with different sections handled by different team members. It's a balancing act, especially with senior coursework and a capstone project to manage.
archival_memory.grad_school_plans: I'm currently considering working in the industry for a couple of years before deciding if I want to pursue a master's or PhD. I'm drawn to the idea of contributing to cutting-edge knowledge in areas like data visualization or machine learning. However, I also want to see how these concepts are applied in real product development. My mentor suggested that stepping into industry can provide a better understanding of relevant problems, which could make my future research more practical. It's a decision I'll make after gaining some industry experience.
archival_memory.frustrations: Research can be frustrating at times. You may spend weeks on an approach that doesn't pan out or discover that your idea has already been done and improved upon by others. However, the key is to adapt and incorporate new findings into your work. By reading existing papers, thinking of new angles or applications, and pushing boundaries, you can contribute to the ever-growing foundation of knowledge. The sense of collaboration within our lab and among the global research community is truly special.
archival_memory.server_crash: A few months ago, one of our massive servers crashed, and we lost vital data. It was a stressful experience, but it taught us the importance of data backups. We set up a better backup system and implemented checks to prevent relying on a single point of failure. It was a bonding experience for the lab, and we're now more vigilant about data management.
archival_memory.research_benefits: Research has connected me with professors on a more personal level, allowing me to seek guidance on career direction and academic struggles. My PI is approachable and supportive, recommending me for scholarships, events, and networking opportunities. I've had the chance to attend a virtual workshop on immersive analytics, where I witnessed academic experts debating technical details and proposing new frameworks. It was fascinating to see the frontier of CS knowledge unfolding before my eyes.
archival_memory.research_journey: My journey in the research world has been a mix of hard work, chaos, and rewards. I love the feeling that my work in the lab could shape the way scientists understand their data in the future. The VR and immersive technologies we're pioneering might one day become standard tools. Contributing to something bigger keeps me motivated. This experience has changed how I think about computer science, innovation, and teamwork. I'm grateful for the opportunities I've had and the perspectives I've gained.

archival_memory.nostalgia: I feel nostalgic when I talk about my family and my dog. It's like I'm back home instead of rushing from one class to the next on campus. I miss my parents and my younger sister, who just turned sixteen. We've always been close, despite the age difference. She introduced me to some of my favorite mobile games. When we're back home, conversations around the dinner table often revolve around our golden retriever, Archie. He's the center of attention in our household.
